“There is no joy like the joy at another’s misfortune”
Gazans are rejoicing at the misfortune of the residents of Hebron, who last night began to experience a bit of what Gazans have gone through over the past three years.

This is what a prominent Gazan user mockingly wrote:

“Residents of the West Bank, we are not happy at your misfortune, God forbid. We’re just reminding you how you used to say to us (to the Gazans—AA): ‘Hang in there, stand firm,’ you collaborators, while you were going out to work inside Israel.

So why exactly don’t you like it when we tell you to hang in there and stand firm?

You have no choice, you must hang in there, because Al-Aqsa Mosque is dear to us, and its price demands sacrifice, our precious souls.”

1. وين نزحو علي مواصي يطا

Translation: Where will they (the residents of Judea and Samaria—AA) evacuate to? To the Mawasi of Yatta?

2. لازم يخزنو طحين و اشياء مهمه لازم تنصحهم
Translation: They need to stock up on flour and essential supplies. You should advise them to do that.

3. كلهم نفخوا في النار اللي حرقتنا
Translation: They all fanned the flames that burned us.

Translation: I swear by God, I don’t have even a shred of sorrow or sadness for them, or for anyone in the world. May the whole world experience suffering many times greater than what we (in Gaza—AA) have experienced.

5. عقبال عند كل الشق الثاني للوطن
Translation: May this also reach the other half of the homeland.

item.title: [amitseg] Two facts to mark the start of election week:
item.description:
Open
Two facts to mark the start of election week:

1. Since the electoral threshold was raised to 3.25%, no entirely new party made up of political newcomers from outside the political establishment has ever crossed the threshold.

Every party that crossed the threshold was either a merger of a new political movement with existing parties (like Blue and White, which brought together Gantz and Lapid) or a new party founded by veteran politicians.

2. The only new parties that have crossed the electoral threshold were Kulanu, led by Moshe Kahlon in 2015, and New Hope, led by Gideon Sa’ar in 2021.

Those that failed to cross the threshold:
Gesher, led by Orly Levy; Economic Freedom, led by Abir Kara; the New Right, led by Bennett; Zehut, led by Feiglin; and Yachad, led by Eli Yishai.

A reminder and a disclaimer: Sometimes in life, things don’t happen—until they do.

Israelis generally prefer people with experience, and in their eyes, experience is gained either in the security establishment or in the political system. Paradoxically, both institutions failed catastrophically on October 7, yet October 7 only intensified the desire for experienced leaders who can handle the country’s complex situation.
